chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hajjaj narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Kufi, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'A large amount of wealth accumulates with me, and it remains for about a year; should I pay zakat on it?' He said, 'No. For everything that has not completed a full year (hawl) in your possession, you are not obligated to pay zakat on it. And for everything that is not rikaz (buried treasure), there is no obligation on you regarding it.'
I said, 'What is rikaz?' He said, 'The silent (uncoined) engraved (gold/silver).'
Then he said, 'When you wish to do that, melt it (coin it), for there is no zakat in the melted gold and silver (bullion/uncoined metal).'
As for jewelry (huliy), there is no zakat in any of it. What indicates this is what has been narrated.

key_terms.حَوْلٌ: A full lunar year of possession

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on paying zakat on gold jewelry and uncoined silver according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the obligation of zakat on gold and silver applies specifically to coined currency (darham/dirham) or melted bullion, exempting uncoined gold and silver known as 'rikaz' or 'al-samit al-manqush'. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between wealth held as stored treasure or raw material versus liquid, circulating capital, thereby relieving the owner of zakat until the metal is processed into a standard form of currency.
